review_notes: I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for other uses of `conjneg` or the same `conj (f (-x))` pattern. The only other file that mentions it is Mathlib/Algebra/Order/Star/Conjneg.lean, which builds on this definition and doesn't compete with it. `conjneg f` is `conj` applied to `f ∘ neg`, which is a composite of existing operations. It is also a named operator that the Fourier-analysis adjoint-of-convolution use relies on, and the file develops a real API around it. That API includes the involutivity lemmas, the compatibility lemmas for sum, prod and support, and `conjnegRingHom`. The rubric says that a named API built from generic operations is not redundant. I found no separate Mathlib definition of the same concept, so I'm not reporting a finding.
